*Galderma Constantly Looking at Potential Acquisitions, CEO Says
Galderma Goes After U.S. Med Spas in Search of Growth — Interview
Galderma Group is pushing further into U.S. medical spas to reach more consumers and drive sales growth.

The Swiss group this week announced its first acquisition since it went public more than two years ago, buying California-based ZO Skin Health for $1.5 billion--including debt--in a bid to broaden its premium skincare portfolio.
Galderma Chief Executive Flemming Ornskov said in an interview that the deal would position the company to help dermatologists and aesthetic doctors get more skincare products in front of consumers.
"We like the fact that it is based in California. We like the fact it's a U.S. company. Why? Because the U.S., for these physician-dispensed products, is a much more developed market," Ornskov said.

Med spas--which offer Botox and other cosmetic drugs--are a fast-growing industry in the U.S. Galderma's anti-wrinkle shots are already present in these spaces, and the company has sought to expand its professional lineup of products.

The company completed in 2022 the acquisition of another California-based skincare brand, Alastin, which is often recommended by physicians or sold in offices that offer laser procedures and plastic surgery. Galderma sees a complement to that franchise in ZO Skin Health.
"We were looking for a product portfolio that would be complementary, but had a lot of the strengths we already saw with Alastin," Ornskov said. "We took a look at what would be scalable."

With the ZO Skin Health deal, Galderma aims to replicate its successful Alastin strategy, though with a portfolio more focused on daily smoothing regimens, analysts at Jefferies wrote in a note to clients.
Ornskov said Galderma still has significant room to grow by making products that are currently in the U.S. available to the rest of the world, but hasn't closed the door on future acquisitions.

"We have many potential drivers of growth, but of course we constantly look at whether there would be opportunities with highly scientifically differentiated products that would fit the image that we want to have," he said.
The company's future merger-and-acquisition activity will likely favor consumer-exposed deals, either in injectable aesthetics or dermatological skincare, analysts at Bank of America said.
